newsitem.title: UK: UK Liberal leader says rivals in chaos over EMU.
newsitem.headline: UK Liberal leader says rivals in chaos over EMU.

text.p: The leader of Britain's minority Liberal Democrats on Sunday attacked the "vacuum of indecision and chaos" within its Conservative and Labour rivals on the proposed single European currency.

In an interview on BBC television, Paddy Ashdown repeated charges he made last week that the refusal by Britain's two biggest parties to state whether they favoured jettisoning sterling was a conspiracy to deceive electors.
"On the biggest issue that confronts this country, the issue which really ought to be addressed, the public are invited to take part in an election in a vacuum," he said.
"This is about the biggest conspiracy of deceit visited on the British people in as long as I can remember," he said.

A general election must be called in Britain by next May, but Labour and the Conservatives have so far maintained that they can only judge whether it would be in Britain's interests to join a single currency when exact details have been thrashed out of how it would work.
Ashdown said by contrast he was certain where the country's interests lay.
"Every single reason that I know for the benefit of this country points me to the position that if a single currency is formed and Britain can be part of it, Britain should be part of it," he said.

"I suspect our position is exactly the chancellor of the exchequer's (Kenneth Clarke's) position though he does not dare to say it," he added. Clarke is widely regarded as the most pro- European member of Prime Minister John Major's cabinet.
Ashdown was Britain's first party leader to pledge a referendum before Britain entered a single currency, a pledge to which Major is now committed. -- London Newsroom *44 171 5427950
